newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB mulling top officials' resignation - paper.
newsitem.headline: DKB mulling top officials' resignation - paper.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) is discussing whether its top officials, including the chairman and the president, should step down to take responsibility for its reported involvement in questionable loans made to a corporate racketeer, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Tuesday.

The Japanese business daily reported in its evening edition that the bank would make a final decision on the issue in the near future, after taking into account internal investigations and an investigation by prosecutors.
A bank spokesman declined comment on the report.
On Tuesday, prosecutors raided the headquarters of the bank in an apparently widening probe into a racketeer payoff scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
DKB has reportedly provided questionable loans to the racketeer at the center of the Nomura's scandal, Ryuichi Koike.
The bank has repeatedly declined comment on DKB's reported link with Koike.
Nihon Keizai said that DKB has provided massive loans to a company linked to the racketeer Koike since 1989, when DKB's president was Kuniji Miyazaki, who is now an adviser to the bank.

In 1994, when DKB reportedly made several more loans to Koike, the bank's president was Tadashi Okuda, who is currently chairman of the bank. Current president Katsuhiko Kondo was senior managing director in 1994.
DKB is also considering internal punishment for bank officials in its general affairs department who had links with the racketeer, it said.
